issues.description: DIRECT_MONOTONIC_BLOCK_SHIFT constant duplicated rather than imported from canonical source.
issues.detail: The constant was previously imported from Lucene99FlatVectorsFormat; the move introduces a fresh copy in Lucene99ScalarQuantizedVectorsFormat with no compiler-enforced link binding the two values. Two independent sources of the same magic number governing on-disk layout can silently drift. Either re-import the original or document the invariant that froze this copy.

issues.description: fieldsWriter throws UnsupportedOperationException instead of expressing read-only-ness in the type system.
issues.detail: Read-only-ness is an essential property of a legacy codec, but it is delegated to a runtime throw discovered at write time rather than encoded statically. A ReadOnlyKnnVectorsFormat base or sealed reader-only variant would let the compiler enforce the precondition. Service-loader registration compounds the trap: users selecting these formats by name fail only at runtime.

issues.description: Constructor still accepts numMergeWorkers and mergeExec that the read-only format silently discards.
issues.detail: Lucene99HnswScalarQuantizedVectorsFormat keeps a constructor accepting numMergeWorkers and ExecutorService, validates them, then discards them since the fields were removed. The signature no longer matches observable state, misleading callers who think they are configuring execution policy. Either remove the parameters or document why a read-only format retains them for ABI compatibility.

issues.description: Protected fields downgraded to package-private on still-public extensible class without documenting the new contract.
issues.detail: OffHeapQuantizedByteVectorValues remains a public abstract class but its members lost protected access. Existing subclasses outside the package silently lose access to state they previously could read. The inheritance contract changed without a stated invariant: either seal the class, document that extension is no longer supported, or restore protected access deliberately.

synthesis.summary: The panel agrees the package move into backward_codecs is mechanically sound and the right direction: legacy formats belong quarantined, and isolating writers into test-only RW shims is a clean decomposition. However, three boundary lapses recur across all reviewers. A duplicated DIRECT_MONOTONIC_BLOCK_SHIFT constant creates two unlinked sources of truth for on-disk layout; read-only enforcement is smuggled into a runtime throw rather than expressed in the type system; and vestigial constructor parameters (numMergeWorkers, mergeExec) survive on a format that has disclaimed writing. A protected-to-package-private visibility downgrade further loosens the inheritance contract without comment. The work is landable once these boundaries are tightened.
